1ede4g9:202: The most important architectural decision of Tarot Pixel is to clearly define the boundary between the engineering layer and the AI layer: the engineering layer handles deterministic work such as pixel-level accurate CSS extraction, mask processing, and layout inference; the AI layer handles judgments that require semantic understanding, such as 'is this layer decoration or content' and 'how does the implementation differ from the design'; the Coding Agent then writes working code using the correct components and architecture in the context of the project codebase. This division avoids handing deterministic work to probabilistic models and avoids handing semantic judgments to rule engines—each layer does only what it does best.

42oni8:241: The core innovation of Tarot Pixel is that it does not aim to 'generate code' but instead lets the Coding Agent understand the design mockup on its own. This Agent-Native design philosophy shifts the tool's role from 'making decisions for the Agent' to 'providing clean information for the Agent.' The system provides visual information on demand via REST API, forming an 'implement → compare → correct' loop rather than one-shot generation. This paradigm shift stems from an understanding of the essence of AI Coding: the Agent already has project context and coding ability; what it lacks is not code generation capability but the ability to use design mockup information reliably.

gb2t4q:192: Traditional D2C platforms use a centralized scaling model—every time a new design pattern is supported, the rule engine and code templates must be updated. Tarot Pixel's Skill model achieves decentralized scaling: the engineering layer provides new data tags or APIs, and the Coding Agent learns how to use them on its own. Model evolution naturally improves understanding and use of Skill documentation, and the system requires no changes for this. The advantage of this decentralized scaling is that as models get smarter, the entire system's visual restoration capability automatically improves.

tc7inf:217: Tarot Pixel abandons the 'one-shot perfect generation' goal long pursued in the D2C field, and instead supports 'conversational iteration.' Even if the first generation is only 80% faithful, the developer only needs to point out 'what doesn't look right / what's wrong,' and the Coding Agent can go back to the design, understand the correction intent, gather more evidence, and complete the changes. Design information stays online continuously; whether for initial implementation or later corrections, the Agent can always revisit the same information source. This is more efficient than pursuing a single perfect generation, because the definition of 'perfect' often depends on project context and cannot be fully covered in one pass.
